q: 1. Quick setting cement is used .....
options: for the construction of structures under water
where resistance to acidic water is required
explain: Quick setting cement sets fast, so it is used for underwater work and in running water where the cement must set before being washed away.

q: 2. Snowcem is .....
explain: Snowcem is a proprietary cement-based paint (coloured cement) used for exterior wall finishing. It is the closest option here.

q: 3. For the manufacture of Portland cement, the proportions of raw materials used, are
explain: Portland cement raw materials are proportioned at roughly 63% lime, 22% silica, and 15% other ingredients.

q: 4. Good quality cement contains higher percentage of
explain: A higher proportion of tricalcium silicate (C3S) gives cement better early strength and overall quality.

q: 5. The percentage of water required for normal consistency for OPC cement, is
explain: For OPC, the standard consistency test typically requires water content between 26% and 33% by weight of cement.

q: 6. Apparatus for Soundness test of cement is
explain: Le Chatelier's apparatus measures cement paste expansion, used to determine soundness.

q: 7. The expansion in portland cement can be tested by .....
explain: The soundness test (Le Chatelier apparatus or autoclave) measures expansion due to free lime and magnesia.

q: 8. Ultimate strength to cement is provided by .....
explain: Dicalcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly and is responsible for the later (ultimate) strength.

q: 9. Sand is mixed with lime mortar is to
explain: Sand added to lime mortar mainly serves to prevent excessive shrinkage and cracking during setting.

q: 10. The lime suitable for making mortar is
explain: Hydraulic lime contains silica and alumina, allowing it to set under water or in damp conditions, making it ideal for structural mortar.

q: 11. The lime suitable for use under water is
explain: Hydraulic lime has the property of hydraulicity, meaning it can set and harden even in the absence of air or submerged in water.

q: 12. Lime containing CaO and set in water is called under normal condition
explain: Lime that possesses the ability to set under water due to the presence of clay and silica is classified as hydraulic lime.

q: 13. As per IS specification, the minimum time for initial setting of ordinary portland cement is
explain: IS codes specify that OPC must have an initial setting time of at least 30 minutes to allow for mixing and placement.

q: 14. The undesirable properties of cement is due to formation of
explain: Tricalcium Aluminate (C3A) is responsible for high heat of hydration and susceptibility to sulphate attack, which are often considered undesirable in large quantities.

q: 15. During production of cement raw materials are mixed in
explain: Ball mills use steel balls to grind and mix raw materials (dry or wet) into a fine powder or slurry.

q: 16. The excess quantity of CaCl2 (>2 %) and triethanolamine (>0.06%) admixtures behaves like a
explain: While small amounts of Calcium Chloride accelerate, excessive amounts can interfere with the setting process and act as a retarder or cause durability issues.

q: 17. Slacking of lime is affected by .....
explain: As per the answer key, slaking is done by adding water, i.e. immersing the lime in water.

q: 18. Which of the following cement is expected to have the highest compressive strength after 2 hours?
explain: High alumina cement develops very high early strength rapidly, reaching much of its strength within hours of setting.

q: 19. The amount of pozzolona in portland pozzolana cement is
explain: Standard PPC usually contains between 15% and 35% pozzolanic material; the key identifies 20-30% as the target range.

q: 20. The commonly used lime in white-washing, is .....
explain: Fat lime, being pure and white, is commonly used for white-washing.

q: 21. Lime concrete is generally used for .....
explain: As per the answer key, option b. Note: lime concrete is also used for wall foundations, so this key answer looks doubtful.

q: 22. The raw materials having more than 10% proportion in the manufacture of cement are
explain: Lime (CaO, 60-67%) and Silica (SiO2, 17-25%) are the two largest components of Portland cement.

q: 23. The temperature range at which the consistency test is conducted
explain: Vicat apparatus tests for consistency are standardized to be conducted in a room temperature range of 27 ± 2°C.

q: 24. The consistency test is performed to find
explain: The standard consistency test determines the percentage of water required to produce a cement paste of standard viscosity.

q: 25. For normal consistency, the penetration in Vicat apparatus should be between
explain: Standard consistency is achieved when the Vicat plunger penetrates to a point 5-7mm from the bottom (33-35mm from top).

q: 26. Le-Chatelier's apparatus is used to carry out
explain: The Le-Chatelier test measures the expansion of cement to ensure it does not undergo delayed volume changes (soundness).

q: 27. Rapid hardening cement attains early strength due to
options: larger proportion of lime grounded finer
small proportion of lime grounded finer
presence of excess percentage of gypsum
explain: Increased lime content (higher C3S) and very fine grinding accelerate the hydration rate and early strength.

q: 28. The commonly used raw material in the manufacture of cement, is .....
explain: Limestone provides the lime, the main raw material of cement.

q: 29. Lime is considered to be hydraulic lime when it sets under water within
explain: Hydraulic lime is defined by its ability to set and harden under water within about 7 to 30 days.

q: 30. The setting time of concrete is reduced during summer due to
explain: High temperature, wind, and low humidity all accelerate moisture evaporation and hydration, reducing concrete's setting time in summer.

q: 31. The cement mortar mix generally used for external plaster
explain: External plaster requires high resistance to weathering; a 1:4 mix is typically used to ensure durability and water-tightness.

q: 32. Which of the following cements contains maximum percentage of dicalcium silicate?
explain: Low heat cement contains a higher proportion of slow-hydrating dicalcium silicate (C2S) to reduce heat generation.

q: 33. The fat lime swells ....... times of its original volume during slaking
explain: Fat lime, being pure and highly reactive, swells to about four to five times its original volume when slaked with water.

q: 34. Gypsum is a
explain: Gypsum is a chemically precipitated sedimentary rock, formed from the evaporation of mineral-rich water.

q: 35. Surkhi is added to lime mortar to .....
explain: Surkhi is a pozzolana; it gives hydraulic properties to lime mortar.

q: 36. The role of super plasticizers in a cement paste is to .....
options: disperse the particles and to remove air bubbles
disperse the particles, removes air bubbles and to retard setting
explain: As per the answer key, option c. Super plasticizers disperse cement particles, release trapped air and can retard setting.

q: 37. Quick setting cement is used:
options: for the construction of structures under water
where resistance to acidic water is required
explain: Quick setting cement, which hardens rapidly, is useful for underwater construction where fast setting is advantageous.

q: 38. As the cement sets and hardens it generates heat. This is called
explain: The heat released during the chemical hydration reactions of cement is termed the heat of hydration.

q: 39. The solvent used in cement paints is
explain: Cement paint is supplied in powder form and mixed with water for application.

q: 40. The commonly used cement in making cement paints is
explain: White cement is used as the base for cement paints to allow for a wide range of pigment colors.

q: 41. The most effective method to reduce the cracking tendency of the concrete is to reduce the
explain: Lowering the water-cement ratio reduces the amount of free water that evaporates, which in turn reduces drying shrinkage and cracking.

q: 42. All burnt bricks should be soaked in water for at least ............ hours to be used with cement mortar.
explain: The key indicates 1/4 (0.25 hours or 15 minutes), though field practice often recommends longer, this value is extracted from the provided answer key.
